findings.title: website_name is not in untrusted_attributes, so it leaks the hidden website for TL0 users
findings.body: `website` is in the `untrusted_attributes` list, so it is omitted for TL0 users when the viewer is anonymous (`scope.restrict_user_fields?`). The new `website_name` attribute is not in that list. It is still serialized, and it carries the host and sometimes the path of the very website that was meant to be hidden. The template now renders `model.website_name` instead of the old controller property derived from `model.website`. Before this change a hidden website produced no name at all, so this is a regression in the spam-protection behaviour. Add `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` and to the matching list in the spec.

findings.title: include_website_name is missing the trailing '?' so it is never called
findings.body: ActiveModel::Serializers only consults `include_<attr>?` methods. The method is defined as `include_website_name` without the `?`, so it is dead code and the attribute is always emitted. When there is no website, `website_name` is serialized as `null` instead of being omitted. The guard also would not have covered the restricted-user case, because it checks `website.present?` and not `scope.restrict_user_fields?`. Rename it to `include_website_name?`, or drop it and use `untrusted_attributes` instead.

findings.title: website_name is now a static server value and goes stale after the user edits their website
findings.body: The old `websiteName` was a client computed property depending on `model.website`, so it updated as soon as the website changed. `website_name` is now a plain attribute that is only set by `findDetails`. `User.save` sends `website` but only copies `bio_excerpt` back from the response. After a user changes their website in preferences and returns to their profile, the same user model is reused. The profile then shows the old `website_name` until a full reload, while the link `href` already uses the new `website`. Refresh `website_name` from the save response, or keep deriving it client-side.

findings.title: Fragile host-matching logic; `"." << website_host` mutates a string literal
findings.body: `"" << website_host` appends to a string literal. This works only while string literals are not frozen; with `frozen_string_literal` or a newer Ruby it raises `FrozenError` and breaks serialization of every user with a website. Use `".#{website_host}"` instead. The same-label-count branch compares everything after the first label. That treats unrelated sites on a shared public suffix as siblings, for example `foo.co.uk` and `forum.co.uk`, and shows the full path. The code also parses the URI up to three times per call; parse it once into a local.

findings.title: Missing tests for the sibling-subdomain branch, blank website, and untrusted users
findings.body: The new tests cover only three of the branches in `website_name`: a different domain, an identical domain, and a parent domain. They do not test the `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com` branch (same label count, shared parent), a blank or unparseable website, or the TL0-anonymous case. The `untrusted_attributes` list at line 11 omits `website_name`, so the information leak described above is not caught. Add cases for these paths.
